purpose: Strengthen the registry-map and boundary proposition using a current primary Irish judgment while preserving its factual limits.

primary_authority.case: O'Flaherty & Ors v Permanent TSB Public Ltd Company & Ors [2026] IEHC 74

verified_observations: The judgment records an express allegation that a Land Registry map was incorrect.
The dispute involved folios created by severance and questions concerning what land fell within the registered folios.
The judgment records a claimed boundary problem and an alleged easement/landlocked-land issue.

The court did not treat the existence of the folio/map as automatically resolving every underlying boundary or easement issue; the factual and legal material presented was insufficient for the plaintiffs' requested relief.

statutory_connection.s85: The current statutory framework provides that, except as provided by the Act, the register/map description is not conclusive as to boundaries or extent.
statutory_connection.s86: The Act contains a specific mechanism by which certain ascertained boundaries can become conclusive.

safe_public_proposition: A Land Registry map/title plan is important evidence of the registered parcel, but it should not automatically be presented as a definitive answer to every physical-boundary, easement or historical-conveyance question.
remaining: Additional primary authorities specifically interpreting ss.84-86.
Historical boundary authorities where the relevant conveyance predates current legislation.
guardrails: No universal boundary rule inferred from one case.
No individual property boundary is determined.
Physical reality, deeds, folio and map remain separate evidence layers.
